messages.cli.update_help.update: Upgrade this install from PyPI. Not the lop-update script, which rebuilds the global runtime from a local git checkout.
messages.cli.update_help.check: Print installed vs PyPI; do not install
messages.cli.update_help.from_snapshot: Install a local source tree (a directory, or a git ref of the current repository) into its own install generation. On macOS, a ref that is exactly a published release installs the published wheel from PyPI — the only build carrying the macOS key agent — and every other ref is built from source.
messages.cli.update_help.allow_downgrade: Allow --from-snapshot to install a build OLDER than the current install (a deliberate rollback; recorded in the install marker). Without --from-snapshot it is refused on the PyPI path, which only installs newer versions; the refresh flags take precedence.
messages.cli.update_help.no_services: Do not bring the `lop serve` daemons onto the new build; the supervised daemons are still repaired. Use this only when something else will start the serves, e.g. a script that owns their launch.
messages.cli.update_help.no_roll: Do not queue a mesh rollout for this update, whatever `network.rollout_on_update` says; `lop network update` still rolls by hand.
messages.cli.services_help.services: Bring this machine's non-runtime services (serve daemons and the supervised daemons) onto the current build, without stopping any running conversation
messages.cli.services_help.services_description: Everything local_operator runs for this machine that is not a conversation. A 'service' is a `lop serve` daemon or a supervised LaunchAgent — the mobile relay, the browser bridge, the tunnel and the wakes agent. Runtimes — the processes holding your conversations — are never stopped: 'restart' reloads a serve daemon in place, keeping its pid and socket.
messages.cli.services_help.status: Report each non-runtime service, the build it is serving, and the build the install is on
messages.cli.services_help.status_description: Read-only. Names the build the install is on and, for each `lop serve` daemon, the build it is SERVING — both sides of every comparison, because the ordinary drift on this machine is a same-version rebuild where the version alone cannot show that a daemon is behind.
messages.cli.services_help.restart: Move every service onto the current build (never stops a runtime)
messages.cli.services_help.wait: How long to wait for an asked daemon to come back on the new build (default: 45s; must be positive). A daemon that does not make it is reported, left serving the build it loaded, and retried by the next `lop services restart`.
messages.cli.services_help.reclaim: End a `lop serve` daemon that is recorded but not serving its address (never one that is serving)
messages.cli.services_help.reclaim_description: Ask ONE serve daemon, named by pid, to leave, escalating from SIGTERM to SIGKILL at a bound, after proving the process is this product's serve daemon and that it is not the one serving the address its record names. `lop services status` lists the daemons this is for. It is never automatic: the daemon may be supervising session runtimes, and no reader of a record can prove a successor is ready to take its place.
messages.cli.services_help.pid: The daemon's pid, exactly as `lop services status` prints it
messages.cli.install_help.install: Manage the local install generations (layout for the stable `lop` runtime)
messages.cli.install_help.prune: Delete install generations nothing is running from
messages.cli.install_help.keep: How many unreferenced generations to keep (default: %(default)s; 0 or more). A generation named by a live or saved session, and the one `current` points at, are never removed
messages.cli.install_help.migrate: Copy this install into the generation layout and point `current` at it
messages.cli.install_help.status: Show the install layout: pointer, generations and what a new `lop` would load

wait_source:
"How long to wait for an asked daemon to come back on the new build "
            f"(default: {DEFAULT_SERVICES_WAIT_S:g}s; must be positive). A daemon that does "
            "not make it is reported, left serving the build it loaded, and retried by "
            "the next `lop services restart`."
